title: Valid Triangle Number
summary: Given an integer array, count the number of triplets that can form a triangle by using their values as side lengths.
statement: Given an integer array, count the number of triplets that can form a triangle by using their values as side lengths.
constraints: Count index triplets whose three lengths satisfy the triangle inequality.
hints: Sort first so one inequality controls the search.
Fix the largest side and move two pointers inward.
When left+middle exceeds right, add every index from left through middle-1.
Sorting makes every larger left value valid once the smallest current left is valid.
editorial: The independent oracle enumerates value triples; the reference uses sorted two pointers.

tests.explanation: The valid triplets are 2,3,4 twice and 2,2,3.
1+2 is not greater than 3, so none form a triangle.
